texts.orig: Intakes can be either ARZ, which is the preferred configuration, or standard The ARZ intake uses Zirconia bearings and sleeves to better protect against abrasive wear and lateral vibration.  This is important near a protector seal.

texts.orig: A gas separator is still an intake, but with some special features designed to keep free gas from entering the pump.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Original gas separator designs were based on increasing gas separation by forcing the fluid flow to reverse in the wellbore. This is where the name of this type of gas separator, REVERSE FLOW,

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Since this type of gas separator does no real "work" on the fluid, it is also called a "static" gas separator.
texts.text: Since this type of gas separator does no real "work" on the fluid, it is also called a "static" gas separator.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Reverse Flow Gas Separator As well fluid enters the gas separator it is forced to change direction.  Some of the gas bubbles continue to rise instead of turn or rise inside of the gas separator, exit the housing and continue to rise.
texts.text: Reverse Flow Gas Separator As well fluid enters the gas separator it is forced to change direction.  Some of the gas bubbles continue to rise instead of turn or rise inside of the gas separator, exit the housing and continue to rise.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The rotary gas separator design works in a similar fashion to a centrifuge.  The first model had centrifuge "paddles" spinning at 3500 rpm and was believed to cause the heavier fluids to be forced to the outside, through the crossover and up into the pump, while the lighter fluid (vapor) stays toward the center, and exits through the crossover and discharge ports back into the well.

texts.orig: The primary aim of the Advanced Gas Handling system is to avoid "gaslocking" in the pump which can result in inefficient cyclical operations and possible premature mechanical failure if not properly controlled.
texts.text: The primary aim of the Advanced Gas Handling system is to avoid "gaslocking" in the pump which can result in inefficient cyclical operations and possible premature mechanical failure if not properly controlled.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AGH does not separate gas but conditions it so it can be produced by the pump.
texts.text: The AGH does not separate gas but conditions it so it can be produced by the pump.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AGH improves the overall efficiency of many submersible lift systems in comparison to those employing gas separators only. In many cases, the AGH will allow successful production of wells that previously could not be economically or reliably produced with submersible pumps employing gas separators due to gas problems.
texts.text: The AGH improves the overall efficiency of many submersible lift systems in comparison to those employing gas separators only. In many cases, the AGH will allow successful production of wells that previously could not be economically or reliably produced with submersible pumps employing gas separators due to gas problems.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AGH results in stable operation with reduced restarts due to underload shutdown (i.e. gas lock).  This improves production and enhances reliability .
texts.text: The AGH results in stable operation with reduced restarts due to underload shutdown (i.e. gas lock).  This improves production and enhances reliability .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AGH is designed to improve the overall lift efficiency of a submergible lift installation by maintaining a higher gas to liquid ratio in the tubing string. The higher GLR will in act to reduce the hydraulic horsepower required to lift an oil well producing oil, water and gas.
texts.text: The AGH is designed to improve the overall lift efficiency of a submergible lift installation by maintaining a higher gas to liquid ratio in the tubing string. The higher GLR will in act to reduce the hydraulic horsepower required to lift an oil well producing oil, water and gas.

texts.orig: Subsea Wells Packers should always be installed above the pumping unit in subsea wells.  A Poseidon  allows all the gas to be produced through the pump into a common production tubing and umbilical.  This reduces installation complexity and expense.

texts.orig: In horizontal completions the wellbore actually runs parallel with the producing formation.  If the wellbore is running updip, gas accumulation in the casing can cause many production problems including slug flow which can lock a pump.  A Poseidon can eliminate these problems.
